checked.found: Shillibeer's horse omnibus began 4 July 1829 between Paddington (Yorkshire Stingo) and the Bank; he was a coachbuilder.
New York and Harlem Railroad horsecar ran on the Bowery from Prince St, first ride 14 Nov 1832, public service 26 Nov 1832; called the world's first street railway (one source hedges 'possibly').
First trial run 2 Aug 1873, passenger service 1 Sept 1873; first successful cable street railway. Both in 1873.
Sprague's Richmond Union Passenger Railway began Feb 1888 (some say regular service May 1888); described as the first large-scale electric streetcar system.
City and South London Railway opened 1890 (formal 4 Nov, public 18 Dec), world's first deep-level electric tube.
Millennium Underground opened May 1896 under Andrassy ut for the millennial celebrations; first underground electric railway on the European continent.
Line 1 opened 19 July 1900 during the Exposition Universelle.
IRT opened 27 Oct 1904, City Hall to 145th St and Broadway, public from 7 pm.
Line A opened 1 Dec 1913 (public 18 Dec); first underground in Latin America and the Southern Hemisphere.
Sol-Cuatro Caminos inaugurated 17 Oct 1919 by Alfonso XIII (public 31 Oct), about 3.5 km.
Ueno-Asakusa (2.2 km) opened 30 Dec 1927, billed as Asia's first subway.
First line opened 15 May 1935; stations conceived as 'palaces for the people' with marble and chandeliers.
Yonge subway opened 30 March 1954, Canada's first subway.
Year 1955 (Line B, Termini-EUR) is supported. But sources attribute the slow build to WWII stalls (and archaeology for Line A, opened 1980), not clearly to ruins on Line B.
checked.suggestion: Drop the ruins claim, e.g. 'Rome opened its first metro line, linking the central station with a planned district south of the city.'

checked.found: Opened 14 Oct 1966 ahead of Expo 67; rubber-tyred; stations with individual art/design.
Line 1 opened September 1969; Lance Wyman's icons helped riders with limited literacy.
Year 1974 is right (express bus system started 22 Sept 1974). But the raised tube stations came later (about 1991-92, possibly 1980s), so the description implies they launched with it.
checked.suggestion: Drop the tube-station claim, e.g. 'A Brazilian city launched dedicated bus lanes, a model copied by cities worldwide.'

checked.found: First 4.6-mile segment opened 27 March 1976; Weese's coffered vaults.
Kwun Tong line opened 1 Oct 1979, first MTR line.
Expo Line opened 11 Dec 1985 (revenue service Jan 1986) for Expo 86; fully automated, driverless.
First section Yio Chu Kang-Toa Payoh (about 6 km) opened 7 Nov 1987.

Year 1993 is right (Line 1 southern section, 28 May 1993). The 'longest metro network in the world' claim is contested: it held that title from about 2010, but current Wikipedia ranks it second by route length.
checked.suggestion: Soften, e.g. 'the start of one of the longest metro networks in the world.'

checked.found: Opened December 2000; inspired by Curitiba's BRT.
Red Line opened 9 Sept 2009, driverless; recognised as the world's longest automated network (Guinness 2012).
Sydney Metro Northwest opened 26 May 2019, Australia's first driverless metro.
